observation.visible_scene: A frothy bright-green liquid is poured into a speckled gray ceramic cup. The excerpt contains an editing cut: the first four frames (t=0–0.25s) show a side view of a sweater-clad hand tilting a clear glass vessel, the stream falling into the cup against blurred green foliage; from frame 5 (t=0.33s) onward the viewpoint jumps to a top-down close-up of the same cup sitting on a plain gray surface, with only the falling stream and the cup interior visible.
visible_changes: A hard cut (not continuous motion) changes the camera angle from a side view to a top-down view between t=0.25s and t=0.33s.
In the top-down shot a thin, steady stream of green liquid falls continuously into the cup for the entire remaining duration.
The pool of green liquid inside the cup visibly grows/rises over time, its surface covered with fine foam and scattered bubbles.
The landing point of the stream drifts: roughly centered early on, it shifts toward the left inner wall around t=1.5–1.8s, then returns to a near-center position for the rest of the clip.
The cup stays centered and stationary in frame; the gray background surface remains uniform, indicating little or no camera movement in the second shot.
The source vessel is out of frame in the second shot; only the green stream and, at the top edge, a small green blob (the lip of the vessel) are intermittently visible.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the pouring began before t=0 or ends after t=3.34s (the action is already underway at the start and still ongoing at the end).
What happens to the hand and glass vessel after the cut, since they leave the frame.
The exact identity/material of the green liquid and of the vessels.
uncertain_details: Minor apparent jitter in the top-down frames could be slight camera shake or natural stream wobble; the cup's position is otherwise stable.
The leftward shift of the stream is a small positional change of the falling column, not a change in the cup or background.
